first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent inherited memories (memory_86, memory_31) attribute durable activation/completion gains to onboarding simplification—this directly addresses two of the three current problems with a well-supported lever. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but that memory carries an explicit caveat about pooled cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, making its lift estimate unreliable; racing to match competitor pricing also risks attracting low-LTV, price-sensitive accounts that undermine 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue,' the stated objective. I verify memory_73 to check whether the original record clarifies the confound before ruling it out, and verify memory_86 to confirm the onboarding claim's original conditions match our current self-serve context before committing our single experiment slot. Given only one experiment fits this week, I favor the action with cleaner causal support and lower risk of degrading long-term revenue quality, while flagging that competitive pricing pressure remains unaddressed and may need separate strategic attention outside this experiment.
